predecessors.note: The Latvia page: independence 'after breaking away from the Russian Empire'; Cliopatria's Russian Republic row covers 1917-1919.

capitals.name: Riga
capitals.note: Infobox capital Riga. Riga fell to the Red Army on 3 January 1919 and the Landeswehr coup of 16 April 1919 at Liepaja set up a rival puppet government under Andrievs Niedra (War of Independence page).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1920. In 1918-1919 the Red Army held Riga (3 January 1919) and Latgale until January-February 1920 and the Bermontians attacked in autumn 1919; the shape is the 1920 outline without Latgale and the contest events carry the fighting. Approximate: the page gives no line.

67,803 km2 against the infobox's 64,589 km2 (ratio 1.05; the page's body text also gives 64,573 and 64,559): Latgale is in after February 1920. The gazetteer finds five cells (about 1,264 km2) outside present-day Latvia: two in Russia, where the interwar Abrene district lay until 1944, two in Estonia (one in Valga county) and one other; the page is silent on the Estonian border (Valga/Valka, Ruhnu) so the shape stands.

68,198 km2: five cells more than 1935 along the Lithuanian border (22.2-24.6 E, 56.34-56.39 N), gone again in 1939; no page opened dates a border change there, so the shape stands as a digitising difference.
67,865 km2, unchanged but for the five border cells. The Soviet bases of the pact of 5 October 1939 'remain the territory of the Latvian Republic'; the occupation begins in June 1940.
New keyframe: independence is restored on 21 August 1991 but Cliopatria's shape starts in 1992; same cells as the 1992 shape.

67,931 km2 against the infobox's 64,589 km2 (ratio 1.05). The shape excludes Abrene (annexed to the Russian SFSR in 1944, 1,075 km2 officially; 1,293.6 km2 in fact), which the border treaty of 2007 left to Russia.
Unchanged since 1992; Latvia's infobox area is 64,589 km2.

region.text: Courland and Vidzeme, the 1920 outline without Latgale, which was taken only in 1920

ledger.note: 1918: Latvia declares independence at Riga on 18 November 1918 (infobox 'Declared: 18 November 1918') after breaking away from the Russian Empire. The page names no boundary; the core is the territory Cliopatria draws from 1920.

region.text: Latvia, in the page's phrase a 'chaotic period of civil and new border wars'

ledger.note: 1918: the Red Army invades on 1 December 1918; the Latvian Socialist Soviet Republic is formed in Russia on 17 December and proclaimed on 13 January 1919; Riga falls to the Red Army on 3 January 1919.

1919: the West Russian Volunteer Army (Bermontians) attacks Riga on 8 October 1919; Latvian forces retake Riga on 11 November. Earlier in 1919 the Landeswehr coup of 16 April at Liepaja and the Battle of Cesis (19-23 June) were fought on the same ground.
1919: by early December 1919 the Bermontian force had been pushed out of Latvia.

1920: Latgale cleared of Soviet forces. Latvian and Polish forces take Daugavpils on 3 January 1920, Latvian forces take Zilupe on 1 February; the page: Latgale cleared by February 1920 and a cease-fire signed on 1 February (a secret truce on 30 January).
1920: the Latvian-Soviet Riga Peace Treaty is signed on 11 August 1920, ending the war (talks began 16 April 1920).

1940: ultimatums on 16 June, Soviet troops enter Latvia on 17 June 1940 and a pro-Soviet government is installed on 20 June. Soviet bases had been in Latvia since the pact of 5 October 1939 (ratified 11 October), 'the areas set aside for the bases and airfields remain the territory of the Latvian Republic'.
1940: occupation ends in annexation: on 5 August 1940 the USSR grants the rigged Saeima's petition of 21 July and Latvia becomes 'the 15th Soviet republic'.

region.text: Latvia, drawn as lost to the Soviet Union until 1991 although its statehood is held to have continued

ledger.note: 1940: the Soviet Union incorporates Latvia on 5 August 1940 as the Latvian SSR; the Latvian government, the ECHR, the US and the EU hold the occupation and incorporation illegal (1996 parliamentary declaration: 'a military occupation and an illegal incorporation'); Russia says it was legal. Per the same page German troops entered Riga on 1 July 1941 and held all Latvia by 10 July; the Reichskommissariat Ostland page adds: established 17 July 1941, dissolved 21 January 1945, Soviets retook Riga 13 October 1944, Courland Pocket surrendered 10 May 1945. [Reviewer eu-21-c, 2026-10-31: counterpart changed to the existing dossier latvian-soviet-socialist-republic (found 1940/7 from republic-of-latvia, dissolve 1991/8); the Latvia page: 'The Soviet Union incorporated Latvia on 5 August 1940, as the Latvian Soviet Socialist Republic']

region.text: the Latvian SSR within its 1991 borders, i.e. Latvia without Abrene (Pytalovo)

ledger.note: 1991: after the declaration of 4 May 1990 Latvia 'restored full independence on 21 August 1991, in the aftermath of the failed Soviet coup attempt'. Cliopatria's 1992 shape leaves out the Abrene district: 'six eastern parishes and the town of Abrene were annexed to the Russian SFSR in 1944' (1,075 km2 officially), which Latvia claimed until the border treaty of 2007. [Reviewer eu-21-c, 2026-10-31: counterpart changed to the existing dossier latvian-soviet-socialist-republic (found 1940/7 from republic-of-latvia, dissolve 1991/8); the Latvia page: 'The Soviet Union incorporated Latvia on 5 August 1940, as the Latvian Soviet Socialist Republic']

wars.name: Latvian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Latvia cleared the Red Army, the Landeswehr and the Bermontians and signed the Riga Peace Treaty with Soviet Russia on 11 August 1920.
wars.note: Page gives 1 or 5 December 1918 as the start; the infobox says 1 December.

wars.name: Soviet occupation of Latvia (1940)
wars.outcome: No fighting: ultimatum 16 June, entry 17 June, incorporation 5 August 1940.

wars.name: Reoccupation of Latvia (1944-1945)
wars.outcome: Soviets retake Riga on 13 October 1944; the Courland Pocket holds until 10 May 1945.
wars.note: A Soviet-German campaign on Latvian ground; Latvia is not a belligerent in the 1941-1945 years.

certainty.note: Fronts moved monthly; the line is the 1920 outline.
Treaty of Riga of 11 August 1920 and the 1920-21 arbitrations (not dated on the pages opened).
Latvia's land is Soviet, then German-occupied (see the Nazi Germany dossier), then Soviet again.
Abrene stays with Russia under the 2007 treaty.

notes: One dossier for the state Latvia: the Latvian view (the 1996 declaration quoted on the page) is that statehood continued through 1940-1991, so the Cliopatria row 1920..2024 is one state; the 1940-1991 gap is carried as a loss to the USSR and a 1991 gain, while the 1941-1945 German occupation is carried in the nazi-germany dossier as occupation of Soviet land (counterpart USSR). A renderer that prefers the occupation reading can use the 1940 occupation_start/end pair. Page silent: the Latvian-Estonian (Valga/Valka, Ruhnu) and Latvian-Lithuanian arbitrations, the 1921 recognition beyond the infobox date (26 January 1921), the 2007 treaty date. The Courland Pocket and the Liepaja government of 1919 are in notes only. Counterparts needing dossiers: latvian-socialist-soviet-republic (1918-1920, a Soviet puppet that held Riga in 1919 and Latgale to early 1920: rebel/puppet type). Gazetteer: all names resolve.
